1.explanation:
In scala.js the CLASS mode controls how class declarations are parsed. Its end regex currently treats the newline before the brace as a terminator and then continues to treat the rest of the line (including “// …”) as part of the class title. That CLASS definition must be adjusted so that comments after the declaration—even when the “{” is on the next line—are correctly recognized by hljs.C_LINE_COMMENT_MODE instead of by the title rule.  

In javascript.js the PARAMS mode governs highlighting of function‐parameter lists. Although PARAMS.contains includes the comment modes, the arrow‐function rule uses a separate inline params matcher (based on PARAMS) and appears to terminate too early or not re-invoke the comment mode for multi-line parameter lists. Fixing PARAMS (or its use in the arrow‐function grammar) will restore comment highlighting inside parentheses.
1.bug_scenario:
There are two related highlighting bugs.  
1) Scala: when you write a class declaration with the opening brace on the next line, any trailing comment on that first line (e.g. “// Something goes here”) is being picked up as part of the class title instead of as a comment.  In other words, “// Something goes here” is rendered with the ‘hljs-title’ style rather than as a comment.  
2) JavaScript: when you define an arrow function whose parameters span multiple lines (especially with destructuring or default values), any inline //-style comments inside the parameter list are not being recognized as comments and thus are not highlighted.

2.explanation:
• In scala.js, the CLASS definition (the grammar object named CLASS) drives how the class header is matched and how its contents are scoped. Because its begin/end patterns and contains array do not properly allow a stand-alone // comment after the header when the brace is on the next line, the comment tokens fall into the NAME or title pattern instead of hljs.C_LINE_COMMENT_MODE.

• In javascript.js, the PARAMS rule (and its helper array PARAMS_CONTAINS) govern comment highlighting inside parentheses. The fact that comments in deeply nested or arrow-function parameter lists aren’t being picked up means that PARAMS_CONTAINS is missing or mis-scoped for those positions. Adjusting PARAMS_CONTAINS (or injecting hljs.C_LINE_COMMENT_MODE into the arrow-function params variants) will restore proper comment highlighting inside all parameter lists.
2.bug_scenario:
There are two related highlighting problems seen in the screenshots and description:

1. Scala: When a Scala class declaration has its opening brace on the next line, any “// comment” that follows the class header is being parsed as part of the class title rather than as a comment. For example:
   class A  // Something goes here
   {
   }
   renders the “// Something goes here” tokens as hljs-title spans instead of hljs-comment.

2. JavaScript: Single-line comments inside a function’s parameter list (especially nested or recursive/arrow function parameters) are not being recognized as comments. In the example:
   f = (
     // f is a recursive function taking:
     [c,        //   c = next digit character
       ...a],   //   a[] = array of remaining digits
     o = '',    //   o = output string
     S = new Set
   ) => …
   none of those “//”-led lines are highlighted as comments within the params mode.
